pr_title: Fix multiplayer room difficulty range not being updated
pr_body:
Fixes #19601

As suggested in comments of the issue this PR adds `StarRating` to `MultiplayerPlaylistItem` which is then used to display up-to-date information about room difficulty range.

issue_context.title: Multiplayer star rating does not initially update for the host
issue_context.body:
### Type

Cosmetic

### Bug description

If you create a multiplayer lobby, the star rating does not display the actual star rating of the beatmap, but instead shows 0.00

comments:
I've done some digging around, and I think I found the cause of this problem.

https://github.com/ppy/osu/blob/9ac322d337e348f63d824e5995942c2ee367dc2a/osu.Game/Screens/OnlinePlay/Components/StarRatingRangeDisplay.cs#L95-L100

There, it's trying to get beatmaps from room's playlist, but as said in the comment, some beatmaps could be unpopulated. Because the code doesn't check if the beatmap is populated, it sets the displayed difficulty to 0.

Another thing I noticed, while you create the room, you get 3 playlist updates, with one of them containing populated beatmaps. But if you edit the playlist or add/remove beatmaps, the updates won't contain populated beatmaps. So, just checking if beatmaps are populated won't cut it, because if you change the playlist after room creation, the star rating won't update.

We can't really query the API like that comment suggests there. There's a bit of an optimisation where the panels in the queue also don't load/query until they're scrolled to, to avoid querying MB of data at once.

For rooms in the lounge listing... osu-web actually serialises a difficulty range along with the room. `MultiplayerRoom` currently has no such thing.

Options are:
- Add `RoomDifficultyRange` to `MultiplayerRoom`, have `osu-server-spectator` populate it.
- Add `StarRating` to `MultiplayerPlaylistItem`.

Tending towards the second as it's more efficient in all regards. The first means that every playlist update is one more SignalR callback to the client, but it makes the `MultiplayerPlaylistItem` model slightly smaller which probably doesn't account for much overall...

Also have to consider - and this is also something that osu!web doesn't consider - that lazer has many more mod combinations than actually is stored in the database. So _something_ will eventually have to compute difficulties with lazer mods, meaning it may also be an interesting time to make use of `osu-beatmap-difficulty-lookup-cache`.  
But for now I suppose returning the beatmap's unmodded difficulty is fine (as osu-web does).

review_comments:
I'm confused by this. The relevant issue thread considers two options: either the client should be sending this star rating value, or the server should be fetching it from db and populating it server-side. So this is the first, but you also opened https://github.com/ppy/osu-server-spectator/pull/169, which is doing... the second?

What is the reasoning here? And if we're doing server-side anyways, then if I'm honest, I'd rather drop the client-side population and be 100% server-authoritative. While this particular piece of data isn't really sensitive in any way, I'd rather prevent clients from being able to send bogus star ratings if possible.

Client doesn't send anything. `MultiplayerPlaylistItem` is fetched from the server, then it is converted into a `PlaylistItem` via this method. Then the returned object is stored in `MultiplayerClient.APIRoom.Playlist` which is used to populate the final `StarRatingRangeDisplay`.

Perhaps the only real problem is that this method even exists in the first place, since `PlaylistItem` itself has a constructor that takes in `MultiplayerPlaylistItem` and does exactly the same thing as this. If you think this method is problematic, then the same could be said about the change i did to `PlaylistItem`'s constructor.

If you also argue that constructor's change is not good then consider the fact that this method is only used to convert an object from one to another. Such an operation should pass on all available information that is compatible between both objects.
I'm 99% sure we don't need this default `ctor`, but leaving it here because I don't want to accidentally break everything server comms wise.
